help.title: Help
help.subtitle: Choose a topic. We explain it simply.
help.bankWhyText: Salaries in Germany are usually paid into a bank account.
help.bankWhatText: Your account number (in DE it starts with DE).
help.bankStep3: Book an appointment or use the app
help.taxWhatText: A personal identification number in Germany used for tax purposes.
help.taxHowText: Register your address or request the number from BZSt.
help.taxLink: Apply for tax ID / official info (BZSt)
help.permitWhereText: On your residence title or supplementary sheet it often says if and how you may work.
help.permitWhatText: “Employment permitted” usually means work is allowed – check limits. Unsure? Ask the authority or advice centre.
help.permitUnsureText: Do not work without permission. Get official advice.
help.disclaimer: General information, not legal advice. Applies to: Germany.
help.bankIntro: You usually need a bank account so your employer can pay your salary. No specific bank is required.
help.bankDontHave: I do not have an account
help.bankNoExplain: Without an account, salary transfers are difficult. Many banks offer basic accounts.
help.bankNext: Next step: choose a bank and open an account.
help.bankNote: Compare offers. We do not recommend one bank.
help.bankLegalNote: Employers may differ. Ask about payment terms.
help.taxNeedText: Employers often need it for payroll. This is not legal advice.
help.taxWhereText: After registration it often arrives by post. Lost? Apply at BZSt.
help.permitIntro: Are you allowed to work in Germany? Check your residence title or supplementary sheet.
help.permitLegalNote: WorkBridge cannot grant a work permit or say that you may work.
help.cvExplainText: Your CV shows photo, details and experience. In WorkBridge it is built from your profile.
help.addressExplainText: In Germany you must register or re-register when you move.
help.addressNote: Your local residents’ registration office is responsible.
help.languageExplainText: Top right you can change the app language (DE, EN, AR, FA, TR, UK).
help.languageHint: Tap DE/EN/… at the top right and choose your language.
help.otherExplainText: For more questions about work and life in Germany, use official advice centres.

workGuide.introTitle: How can I work in Germany?
workGuide.introText: You want to work in Germany but are unsure what you need? We help step by step. First check this checklist. If something is missing, we show what to do and guide you to the right official place.
workGuide.hello: Hello! 👋 We help you find work step by step.
workGuide.q_idDoc: Do you have a valid ID / residence document?
workGuide.q_permit: Are you allowed to work in Germany?
workGuide.q_tax: Do you have a tax ID?
workGuide.q_bank: Do you have a bank account?
workGuide.where: Where can you do it officially?
workGuide.help_idDoc_what: A valid passport, ID card or residence title shows who you are.
workGuide.help_idDoc_why: Registration, banks and authorities usually need a valid document.
workGuide.help_idDoc_do: Check if your document is still valid. If not, ask the authority or advice centre.
workGuide.help_permit_what: Your residence title or supplementary sheet often states if and how you may work.
workGuide.help_permit_why: Working without permission is risky for you and the employer.
workGuide.help_permit_do: Check your document. Unsure? Ask the foreigners authority or advice – we do not decide for you.
workGuide.help_tax_what: The tax ID is a personal number for taxes in Germany.
workGuide.help_tax_why: Many employers need it for payroll – depending on your situation.
workGuide.help_tax_do: After registration it often arrives by post. Lost? Apply at BZSt.
workGuide.help_bank_what: A bank account for salary transfers. No specific bank is required by default.
workGuide.help_bank_why: Salaries in Germany are usually paid by transfer.
workGuide.help_bank_do: Compare banks and open an account if you do not have one.
workGuide.permitDisclaimer: WorkBridge does not grant work permits or make official decisions.
workGuide.bankDisclaimer: No specific account is required for everyone by law. Ask your employer if needed.
workGuide.statusReady: You are ready for the job search
workGuide.statusCannot: You cannot yet safely confirm whether you may work
workGuide.legalNote: General info for Germany/Hamburg. Not legal advice. If unsure: official office.
